item.title: Sciatic Nerve Slider
clinicalUse: Selected lumbar radicular/sciatic mechanosensitivity when neurological status is stable
patientPosition: Supine SLR or sitting slump-modified position depending on irritability.
therapistPosition: Beside leg or patient in sitting.
contact: Support leg; avoid pressure over posterior knee.
forceDirection: Increase knee extension/hip flexion while reducing ankle or cervical neural load, then reverse.
safety: Do not delay urgent referral for cauda equina/progressive motor loss.
item.visualCue: Knee/hip load ↔ ankle/neck unload; rhythmic, not sustained.

subTechniques.name: Sciatic Nerve Slider — Slump-Based
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve posterior-chain neural movement tolerance without prolonged end-range tension.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Seated slump position modified so symptoms are mild or absent at baseline.
subTechniques.contact: Therapist supports the leg/foot as needed; there is no direct nerve pressure.
subTechniques.direction: Pair knee extension with cervical extension to unload proximally, then knee flexion with cervical flexion to reverse the slider. Keep ankle position neutral initially and add it only if needed.
subTechniques.reassess: Slump/SLR response, leg symptom distribution and sitting/walking tolerance.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The hallmark of a slider is opposite-end movement—one end loads while the other unloads.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop with progressive neurological loss, severe irritability or red-flag spinal symptoms.

subTechniques.name: Tibial Nerve Slider
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve neural movement tolerance into the posterior calf/plantar foot distribution.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the hip/knee positioned below the neural symptom threshold.
subTechniques.contact: Support the limb; ankle/foot motion is controlled without direct pressure behind the medial malleolus.
subTechniques.direction: Use dorsiflexion/eversion as the distal loading component while unloading proximally with knee flexion or reduced hip flexion; then reverse.
subTechniques.reassess: Tibial-biased symptoms, ankle/foot neural response and walking tolerance.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Keep the movement below a lingering symptom threshold; the goal is excursion, not stretch intensity.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid aggressive loading with acute nerve injury or progressive sensory/motor loss.

subTechniques.name: Common Fibular Nerve Slider
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine or side-lying with the knee supported and the limb below the symptom threshold.
subTechniques.contact: Avoid direct compression around the fibular head; control the ankle/foot gently.
subTechniques.direction: Use plantarflexion/inversion as the distal bias while unloading proximally with knee flexion or reduced hip flexion; then reverse the sequence.
subTechniques.reassess: Fibular-biased symptoms, ankle/foot sensation and functional walking.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Because the common fibular nerve is superficial at the fibular head, avoid local pressure there.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop with worsening foot-drop-type weakness or persistent sensory change.

subTechniques.name: Femoral Nerve Slider
subTechniques.patientSetup: Side-lying or prone with the hip and knee positioned below the symptom threshold.
subTechniques.contact: Support the pelvis and distal leg; avoid forcing lumbar extension.
subTechniques.direction: Increase distal load with knee flexion while simultaneously reducing proximal load by decreasing hip extension; then reverse the pair.
subTechniques.reassess: Femoral-biased neurodynamic response, anterior-thigh symptoms and walking/stair tolerance.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Differentiate neural symptoms from simple quadriceps stretch by changing spinal/hip components and observing the response.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid aggressive tensioning with acute femoral neuropathy or progressive weakness.
